initiative.title: Self-hosted team server with Docker Compose
initiative.summary: A free Docker Compose team server for one company: local accounts, projects with author and viewer members, CSV and JSON files by upload or URL, and project folders on one volume. File-only; database sources are a separate initiative.
initiative.next_action: Finish M4 PR; then M5 upgrades.

sources.notes: Hosting-modes initiative somewhat replaces the commercialization initiative, possibly in parallel; separate initiative for a proper app with users, login, config.
No CLI, server, auth, or user model exists.
Loopback-only file server with a per-run token; ProjectFiles port; browser runs the folder codec; SSE change events; apps/app shell with autosave and refused-save handling.

Multi-user.

claims.statement: Analyses and config are stored server-side.
Used within one company by 1–10 authors with 10–100 viewers.

Revenue comes from hosted/self-hosted app plans; component licensing is paused.

claims.statement: Every viewer has an account with a viewer role; no anonymous share links at first.
First sign-in is admin-managed local accounts (email + password); OIDC/SSO later.
Self-hosting is free.
A server holds many projects; each project has members. Author or viewer is set per account; authors create projects.
Saved work is CLI-format project folders on the data volume; accounts and sessions sit in a small database beside them.
Viewers can filter, select, and inspect, but nothing they do is saved.
An admin adds database connections in the UI; the server stores credentials encrypted on the volume.
claims.notes: Database connections are their own initiative (QA-S3 n13).

claims.statement: When two authors edit one analysis, the last save wins and the other author's page reloads with a notice naming who changed it.
A URL source keeps its downloaded copy, shows when it was fetched, and can be refetched; scheduled refetch is an evaluation item.
Authors add files by uploading them or by giving a URL that the server downloads.
An admin grants each database connection to specific projects.
claims.notes: Database connections are their own initiative (QA-S3 n13).

claims.statement: The first team server is file-only: no database sources. Database connections are a separate large initiative.
Admin is a flag on an account; the first account is admin; admins see and manage every project.
URL sources may fetch any http(s) address, including internal ones; metadata and link-local addresses are refused.
Backup is a copy of the data volume; a new image migrates data on start after a dated backup, and refuses to start if migration fails.

shape.appetite: One file-only team server built on the CLI's server, folder codec, and apps/app: accounts, projects with members, upload and URL sources, one Compose service and one volume. No database sources.
shape.problem: A company wants authors to build analyses on a shared server and colleagues to sign in and explore them, without anyone installing the CLI.
shape.recommended_shape: Keep each server project a plain CLI project folder under /data/projects and keep the browser as the folder reader. The server adds three things around the existing ProjectFiles routes: who is asking (session cookie replaces the per-run token), which project (path prefix), and whether they may write (author membership). Accounts, sessions, and members live in SQLite (node:sqlite) at /data/exploreda.db. Started by `exploreda server` from the same bin; the image wraps it.
success_moves: Prove roles on the unchanged ProjectFiles routes with seeded accounts on a local Node run before any Docker or accounts UI.
Run the existing ProjectFiles contract suite against the project-scoped, role-checked adapter so the CLI and server cannot drift.
Hand out one-time set-password links instead of sending email: no SMTP setting, no outbound dependency.
Treat URL sources as files: download into the project's data folder with a small sidecar recording URL and fetch time, so the folder still opens with npx.
Make migration a startup step with a dated backup and refuse-to-start on failure, tested against a fixture volume from the previous version.
Keep the CLI's loopback and token path untouched; team mode is a separate auth adapter selected by the subcommand.

first_proof.question: Do role checks on the CLI's unchanged file routes make apps/app behave correctly for an author and a viewer?
first_proof.artifact: Run apps/app against the Node server in team mode locally (no Docker) with two seeded accounts, an author and a viewer, and one project folder. Observe: The server refuses the viewer's writes and the app shows view-only with no failed-save errors; the author's save reaches the viewer's open page as a reload notice naming the author; the folder still opens with npx exploreda.
first_proof.decision_rule: If role checks on the unchanged file routes hold, build the accounts UI, Compose, and URL sources on them. If the app needs more than refused writes to behave as view-only, add a viewer mode to the app shell first.

rabbit_holes: URL fetch from inside the company network (SSRF): allowed by choice; block metadata and link-local, cap size and time, log fetches.
Cross-site requests once the server leaves loopback: SameSite cookies plus an Origin check against the configured public URL.
Concurrent saves from two authors: last write wins on whole files; relies on the CLI's atomic write and watch reload.
Upload size: the CLI handler caps bodies at 50 MB while CLI data targets about 100 MB; the server needs a streamed upload with a configurable limit.
Migrating the volume across versions without losing projects.

milestones.proof: Handler tests (viewer/non-member/cross-site 403, missing cookie 401, named save broadcast skipping the writer); store contract suite on the in-memory store; saver viewer-mode test; browser two-window check at 1280/783/390.

milestones.rollback: Remove the server subcommand; localAccess path is the old handler.

milestones.title: Admins set up accounts and authors set up projects
milestones.outcome: Accounts persist in SQLite; from an empty data directory an admin sets up the server, invites by link, and authors create shared projects with members.
milestones.proof: Store contract suite on SQLite plus restart persistence; node:sqlite spike; Store and handler tests per rule; browser checks of setup, admin, and members at three widths; pnpm check:ui.
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: Full multi-user server without file intake beyond the app's own saves.
milestones.rollback: Revert the PR; M1 seeded mode remains.
evidence: node:sqlite spike: loads without a flag on Node 22.5+ (experimental warning, suppressed) and on 24; absent on 20, so it loads lazily.

milestones.outcome: Authors upload CSV/JSON or fetch by URL, see fetch time, and refetch.
milestones.proof: Local failing HTTP server tests; blocked-address tests; failed refetch keeps old copy; folder opens with npx.

history.summary: Intent recovered from two handwritten notebook pages and the accompanying chat request.
Three question rounds settled projects with members, folder storage, viewer exploration, upload and URL sources, admin flag, auto-migrate; database sources moved out of scope. Shape brief written.

question_rounds.focus: shape the server work on top of the CLI server

questions.question: How should analyses be shared on a team server?
questions.effect: Server holds many projects; membership per project assigns author or viewer. Resolves the workspace question.

questions.question: Where should a server's saved work live?
questions.effect: Same .eda folders as the CLI under the data volume, reusing ProjectFiles; accounts and sessions in a small SQLite file.

questions.question: What can a viewer do with an analysis?
questions.effect: Viewers get full interaction; the server refuses their writes; nothing persists.

questions.question: Who defines database connections and where do credentials live?
questions.effect: Admin settings page for connections; credentials stored encrypted in the volume; needs an encryption key from the operator.

questions.question: Two authors edit the same analysis. What happens?
questions.answer: Last save wins, with a notice.
questions.effect: Reuse the CLI's outside-change reload over server-sent events, naming who changed it; no locks or live merge.

questions.question: Where do a viewer's database rows come from?
questions.effect: Server keeps the last snapshot per source on the volume; manual refresh plus an optional schedule; the page shows when the data was read.

questions.question: How do files get into a server project?
questions.answer: Author uploads in the app; author provides a URL and the server downloads it (user-added option).
questions.effect: Upload and fetch-by-URL are in. Operator drop-in and CLI project import were not chosen. URL fetch raises internal-network reach and refresh questions.

questions.question: Which projects can use an admin-added connection?
questions.effect: Each connection carries a list of projects allowed to use it.

questions.question: Which URLs may the server fetch, and do URL sources refresh?
questions.effect: Internal URLs allowed; cloud metadata and link-local addresses always refused; the downloaded copy is kept and can be refetched.

questions.question: Who is an admin, and what can they see?
questions.effect: The first account is admin and can grant the flag; admins manage accounts and every project's members.

questions.question: Who can create a project?
questions.effect: Author or viewer is an account-level kind; authors create projects; a viewer account is a viewer in every project.

questions.question: What is the first release worth announcing?
questions.effect: Superseded by n13: DB is not in this initiative at all.

questions.question: Confirm: v1 files-only, URL snapshots, DB connections in the next release?
questions.answer: The initial server does file-only work and does not add database sources; that is its own large initiative.
questions.effect: Database connections, credential storage, and per-project grants leave this initiative. URL refetch kept as a file operation; scheduled refetch moved to evaluate (provisional).

questions.question: What should upgrades and backups look like?
questions.effect: Backup = copy /data; a new image migrates on start after a dated backup of what it changes; refuses to start if migration fails.
